name: Palm Valley Boat Parade
host: the Palm Valley Boat Parade committee
venue: Intracoastal Waterway and Palm Valley Bridge viewing area
address: Palm Valley Bridge viewing area, Ponte Vedra Beach, FL
paras: The Palm Valley Boat Parade lights up the Intracoastal Waterway on Saturday, December 5, 2026, at 6 PM. The parade is free to watch, and the organizers describe it as a local tradition since 1993.

Decorated power boats and sailboats start one mile south of the Palm Valley Bridge and travel north toward Marsh Landing. Docks along the shore compete in a decorating contest, so families see lights on the water and on the banks.
The Palm Valley Bridge viewing area is a favorite gathering spot. The committee asks families to bring a chair and arrive early, and it posts parking and viewing updates on its official viewing page.
tip: Bring a chair and arrive early to claim a spot at the Palm Valley Bridge viewing area.

name: Una Noche de Navidad and Las Posadas at Mission Nombre de Dios
host: the National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche
venue: National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche, Mission Nombre de Dios
address: 101 San Marco Avenue, St. Augustine, FL 32084
paras: The National Shrine of Our Lady of La Leche at Mission Nombre de Dios hosts Las Posadas as a Christmas tradition on Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 3 to 8 PM at 101 San Marco Avenue in St. Augustine.

The tradition dates back to 16th century Mexico and re-enacts the Holy Family's journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem as they look for shelter on the eve of Jesus' birth, celebrating the spirit of Advent.
The shrine's event page links a ticket form and a printable flyer titled Una Noche de Navidad.
tip: Reserve through the ticket form on the shrine's event page before the day.

name: Colonial Night Watch and Torchlight Parade
venue: Oldest House Museum and Colonial Quarter
when_note: Friday, December 4 and Saturday, December 5, public days 10 AM to 4 PM, torchlight parade Saturday at 7 PM
paras: The Historic Florida Militia holds the 2026 St. Augustine Colonial Night Watch on Friday, December 4 and Saturday, December 5 at the Oldest House Museum, with public days from 10 AM to 4 PM both days.
A period encampment recreates the years 1739 through 1785, when Spanish and British forces and their allies were in St. Augustine. Scheduled presentations run Saturday from 11 AM to 3 PM.

The Torchlight Parade starts at the Visitor Information Center on Saturday at 7 PM and passes through the City Gates and down St. George Street to the Governor's House at 48 King Street. A volley of joy follows the parade.
The organizers ask for no live rounds and say musket demonstrations are staged by a safety officer, so younger visitors may want ear protection.
tip: Bring ear protection for little ones, since the muskets fire during the demonstrations and parade.
